task_specification.objective: Let an unarmed player approach a readable Isha, experience the themed D01–D03 rescue-request conversation, accept Q01 once and return safely to exploration; repair the nearby lamp obstruction as its necessary camera dependency.

diagnosis.root_cause: The candidate boots the authored village and unarmed Ranger but its wrapper provides demo controls rather than a reachable Isha conversation, dialogue state or Q01 transition. The selected equipment and teaching gates therefore lack their opening player-facing prerequisite. Separately, environment_quality.gd creates foreground lamp poles and globes; the globe has no matching collision shape. This is a plausible cause of framebuffer obstruction escaping physics visibility samples, but it requires a same-route isolation probe. R04/R22 are unverified qualitative reviews, not executable scenarios or demonstrated failures of every listed behavior.

stop_conditions: Stop scope growth when the opening conversation and its camera dependency are implemented and focused checks are complete; do not add equipment training or another NPC module.
Do not claim R04, R22 or milestone_02 closure from this prerequisite increment.
If a required character, portrait, font or interface resource cannot be qualified through authorized sources, report the exact missing dependency and leave affected acceptance unmet.
If independent ordinary-input replay or state-bound capture is unavailable, preserve completed candidate work and report insufficient evidence separately from product failure.
Do not close the camera finding from physics samples alone or introduce default-startup self-driving tests.
Stop dependent changes if native import/boot or preserved controller behavior regresses; repair that regression before proceeding.

strategy.rationale: Follow the frozen operator revision's first-module priority: build the actual reachable Isha interaction rather than continue controller-only changes or attempt the entire equipment/teaching sequence. Investigate the lamp at its creation and binding boundary by comparing the ordinary wrapper with its optional lamp overlay isolated and the retained authored fixtures. This materially changes the causal strategy from transform tuning and qualification-only observations. The mandatory single-task boundary prevents reopening deferred blocker work this round.

code: Check candidate import/boot and retain native_godot_project and host_godot_boot through the registered Host checks.
Inspect live scene/resource paths, NPC grounding, portrait/font bindings and licenses; do not count unbound files or pool metadata as adoption.
Verify Q01 reward commitment, saved logical node/confirmed choice and pause/input ownership. Preserve remapping, capture cancellation, B-to-U-to-default behavior and E/F reservations.
Require first advance to complete the revealing line and a later deliberate advance to proceed; incomplete text disables choices, and held/repeated input cannot skip or submit twice.
runtime: Host/Tester independently traverses spawn to Isha, attempts out-of-range and obstructed interaction, opens D01–D03, asks an optional question, accepts rescue and exits. Observe unarmed hand/back visuals, actual Q01 state and exactly one 10 XP award.

Repeat interaction, abandon before confirmation, save with an unconfirmed choice, restart/load, and save after acceptance. Restore the logical conversation without automatic choice submission or reward duplication.

During dialogue, verify world movement and active gameplay timers stop while text/UI continue. Open and close a nested menu/save view: world remains paused until the last owner closes; held movement, mouse buttons and E do not leak into exploration.

Repeat the original lamp route using current effective bindings: forward/reverse, yaw approximately -90 degrees, travel toward +X, switch shoulders, sprint, stop near the recorded position and Roll. Host captures distributed action frames paired with actor/camera transforms; include an adjacent near-wall route and recovery to locomotion.
visual: Compare ordinary Isha approach and conversation views with village-dialogue-v1.png for character identity, mature proportions, portrait placement, speaker emphasis, parchment/borders, text hierarchy and choice affordances.

Check long Chinese lines, punctuation, English names and key prompts at 100%, 150% and 200% text scale, with revealing/full text, focused/disabled choices and nested menu states; reject missing glyphs, clipping or overlapping options.

The owning conversation and approach UI must default to a clean player view with contextual objective/interaction cues. Internal camera/animation/asset readouts and inherited demo key walls belong behind an explicit developer-only switch; preserve accessible user-facing control settings.

For new resources, qualify these bounded families in the existing handoff: Isha actor is a justified singleton, one distinct source/runtime variant and maximum share 1.0, mature low-poly village match, complete textured geometry/material/scale evidence, opaque 3D rendering, views at approach/front/side/idle; portraits are a repeated identity family, at least two distinct source/runtime variants, .

done_when: Through ordinary movement and E interaction, an unarmed player can reach Isha, read and choose within the finished D01–D03 conversation, accept Q01 for exactly one 10 XP award, and return to exploration; the same conversation and committed result survive exit, nested save/menu use and restart without accidental submission or repeated rewards.

On the recorded lamp route, fresh shipped-camera sprint, stopped-idle and Roll views show the Ranger's face and central body readable in both shoulders, including the nearby stop around (18.44,-2.8,18.08), with grounded traversal and controllable recovery preserved.
tasks.instructions:
Own only the first Isha conversation and its selected camera dependency. Bind the work to the frozen candidate and operator-development.md: retain Preview.tscn's authored village, Player.tscn, Ranger/head, animation libraries, weapon resources and stable movement interfaces. Allocate R04 to its unarmed rescue-request prerequisite and R22 to its real movement/camera/approach/interaction introduction; explicitly report the remaining equipment and combat-teaching outcomes as unmet.

Place one complete, mature-proportioned Isha actor at a grounded, reachable safe-square approach derived from actual terrain and occupied volumes. Check a usable standing/turning space, line of sight, distance-limited E prompt and return route. Keep the actual prompt and input ownership synchronized; pressing E away from or through an obstacle must not open her conversation. Do not substitute a primitive marker or name label for the character.

Implement D01–D03 using the PRD's facts and choices: four people were abducted, they crossed the bridge toward the forest, accepting rescue points toward Hers and grants Q01's once-only 10 XP. Optional questions do not gate acceptance. Opening or abandoning the conversation must not grant equipment, mark training complete or award XP. Show the actual current objective and a recognizable next landmark; preserve conversation progress and confirmed reward facts without inventing the later Hers module.

Finish the dialogue presentation against village-dialogue-v1.png: illustrated half-body Aelor on the left, Isha on the right, active-speaker emphasis, separate name/body/choice layers, parchment reading surface, fine borders and legible Chinese serif typography. The reference is a composition guide, not a source of baked text or proof of gameplay. Provide distinguishable hover, keyboard focus, pressed and disabled states, restrained entry/exit feedback and appropriate UI sound cues. Reveal approximately 25–35 Chinese characters per second with configurable speed and instant display. First advance only.
